Beyond "Click Here": Crafting Truly Accessible Link Text

2026-05-08 3 min read

Generic link text like "click here" creates significant barriers for users with screen readers and cognitive disabilities. Discover why descriptive link text is paramount for intuitive navigation and learn practical steps to enhance your website's accessibility and user experience.

The ubiquitous "click here," "read more," or "learn more" link text might seem harmless, but it's a major accessibility hurdle. For users relying on screen readers, these phrases strip away crucial context, forcing them to navigate through a disjointed list of identical links. This challenge extends to users with cognitive disabilities, who benefit greatly from clear, unambiguous cues about a link's destination. WCAG 2.4.4 (Link Purpose (In Context)) specifically addresses this need, emphasizing that the purpose of each link should be clear from its text alone or from its programmatically determined link context.

To create truly accessible links, every link's text should clearly describe its destination or purpose. Instead of "Click here to download our report," consider "Download our 2023 Accessibility Report (PDF)." Replace a vague "Learn more" with "Read our full guide to WCAG 2.2 principles." This approach allows all users, especially those using assistive technologies, to understand what to expect when they activate a link, significantly improving navigation efficiency and overall comprehension. Focus on making the link text meaningful even when read out of context.

Implementing descriptive link text is a fundamental step towards a more inclusive website, benefiting not only users with disabilities but also improving SEO and general usability for everyone. Clear links build trust and reduce cognitive load, making your content more accessible and engaging. As you audit your content, challenge every generic link and replace it with text that adds value.
